label: L14 · Endotoxin & Sorting
rows: Endotoxin
LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDE of the outer membrane. LIPID A = biologically active part. Released on LYSIS (including by antibiotics) and during rapid growth.
Three parts
Lipid A (active) · core polysaccharide (same for large groups) · O antigen (unique per organism; repeat number = rough, semi-rough, smooth).
Usually protective
Innate immunity via a lipopolysaccharide binding complex + Toll-like receptor → moderated inflammation keeps mucosal infection mucosal.
Damaging

Complement (hemorrhagic necrosis) · coagulation (disseminated intravascular coagulation, bradykinin) · high levels impair neutrophil CHEMOTAXIS · macrophages release tumor necrosis factor, interleukins 1 and 6.
Low vs flood
Low: fever, malaise, aches. Flood: SEPTIC SHOCK — microthrombi, vasodilation, cardiac output first UP (warm shock), then down → organ failure.
Three sorting properties
OXYGEN requirement · LACTOSE fermentation · OXIDASE enzyme.
Aerobes, no fermentation
Pseudomonas, Burkholderia, Bordetella, Francisella, Brucella, Alcaligenes. Pairs: Pseudomonas + Burkholderia OPPORTUNISTS · Brucella + Francisella ZOONOTIC · Bordetella + Legionella HUMAN.
Facultative anaerobes

Lactose + (coliforms): Escherichia, Klebsiella, Citrobacter, Enterobacter. Lactose −, oxidase −: Salmonella, Shigella, Proteus, Yersinia and others. Lactose −, OXIDASE +: Haemophilus, Pasteurella. Obligate anaerobe: Bacteroides.

label: L14 · Pseudomonas & Its Relatives
rows: Pseudomonads
Small rods, ONE POLAR flagellum · aerobic, NO fermentation · oxidase + catalase + · water-soluble pigments · soil and water.
P. aeruginosa signs
GRAPELIKE odor · greenish-blue pigment PYOCYANIN · resists soaps, quaternary ammonium disinfectants, drying.
Why hospitals
BIOFILMS → contaminates ventilators, intravenous solutions, anesthesia equipment. Major nosocomial agent.
Virulence
Exotoxin A blocks PROTEIN SYNTHESIS · slime layer (anti-phagocytosis, biofilm) · exoenzyme S → T cell APOPTOSIS · multidrug resistant (permeability, enzymes, efflux pumps, gene transfer).
Disease
★ Burns, neoplastic disease, CYSTIC FIBROSIS. Septicemia → endocarditis, meningitis. Healthy people: rash, urinary tract infection, SWIMMER'S EAR, CORNEAL ULCER (contact lenses).
Vaccine
In development, for cystic fibrosis; but in CHRONIC cystic fibrosis infection it may worsen lung inflammation.
Relatives

Obligate aerobes, no sugar fermentation, opportunists. B. cepacia: cystic fibrosis copathogen, mutates fast. B. pseudomallei: MELIOIDOSIS, tropical soil, injury or inhalation. A. baumannii: MONTHS on fomites, combat wounds. S. maltophilia: biofilms on equipment.

label: L14 · Brucella, Francisella, Bordetella, Legionella
rows: Brucella

Tiny coccobacilli. B. abortus (CATTLE), B. suis (PIGS). Malta / UNDULANT / Bang fever: fever fluctuating weeks to a year. Slaughtering, placentas, UNPASTEURIZED dairy. Agglutination titer. ANIMAL vaccine.
Francisella tularensis
TULAREMIA, rabbit fever. Animals, water and dust, vector bites; 10–50 organisms. Ulcerative skin lesion + swollen nodes. Intracellular → RELAPSE. Attenuated vaccine.
Bordetella pertussis
Minute encapsulated coccobacillus. Healthy CARRIERS; contact or aerosols. Binds and destroys CILIATED cells → mucus blocks airways.
Pertussis stages
CATARRHAL (drainage, sneezing, occasional cough) → PAROXYSMAL (persistent cough + the WHOOP).
Pertussis prevention
DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus and acellular pertussis): ACELLULAR, toxoid + antigens, 5 doses 2 months–6 years. Rising: infants under 2 months unvaccinable · WANING immunity · pertactin-negative strains.
Legionella

WEAKLY Gram negative, pleomorphic. Hard to culture: CHARCOAL YEAST EXTRACT agar. Lives with AMEBAS in water. AEROSOLS (cooling towers, fountains). Legionnaires disease, Pontiac fever. Men over 50, smokers, nosocomial elderly.

label: L14 · The Enterics: Traits, Media, Antigens
rows: Family traits
Small non-spore-forming rods · FACULTATIVE anaerobes · ALL ferment GLUCOSE · nitrate → nitrite · OXIDASE − · catalase + · all have O antigen.
Coliform vs not
COLIFORMS ferment LACTOSE; non-coliforms do not.
Two kinds of diarrhea
TOXIGENIC: on the surface, oversecretion of fluid (enterotoxigenic E. coli). INVASIVE: enter the lining, bleeding (Shigella).
Media
EMB (eosin methylene blue) and MacConkey's (crystal violet + BILE SALTS): both SELECTIVE for Gram negatives, DIFFERENTIAL for lactose fermenters (pink on MacConkey's).
Antigens
H = FLAGELLAR · K = CAPSULE/fimbrial (Vi in Salmonella) · O = SOMATIC cell wall, all have it.
Hospitals
With Pseudomonas, almost HALF of nosocomial infections; soap dishes, sinks, catheters, tracheal cannulas.

label: L14 · Escherichia coli Pathotypes
rows: E. coli
Common AEROBIC gut bacterium, but NOT the most prevalent (anaerobic Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium are). Virulence by PLASMID transfer.
Enterotoxigenic
Heat-labile + heat-stable TOXINS → fluid secretion; fimbriae, SMALL intestine. TRAVELER'S DIARRHEA. Fluids; bismuth salicylate counters the toxin.
Enteroinvasive
NO toxins, mechanical damage; LARGE intestine, like SHIGELLOSIS. Bloody diarrhea, high fever.
Enteropathogenic
Adheres and destroys MICROVILLI. Wasting INFANTILE diarrhea, top infant killer worldwide. Prevention: BREAST FEEDING.
Enterohemorrhagic O157:H7

SHIGA toxin binds RIBOSOMES. CATTLE reservoir: beef, water, vegetables; ~100 cells. Hemorrhagic colitis, HEMOLYTIC UREMIC SYNDROME. RAINBOW agar: BLACK colonies (glucuronidase −). Antibiotics may WORSEN it; dialysis, plasmapheresis.
Outside the gut
Most URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (women, catheters) · neonatal meningitis · COLIFORM COUNT = fecal contamination of water.

label: L14 · Other Coliforms & Proteus
rows: Klebsiella pneumoniae
Normal RESPIRATORY flora · LARGE CAPSULE · NOSOCOMIAL PNEUMONIA.
Serratia marcescens
RED pigment PRODIGIOSIN · pneumonia in chronic ALCOHOLICS, burns, urinary tract infections.
Enterobacter · Citrobacter
Opportunistic urinary tract, wound and bloodstream infections.
Proteus
HIGHLY MOTILE, peritrichous flagella → SWARMING waves. Urinary tract infection, bladder and KIDNEY STONES, Crohn's disease.
Providencia · Morganella
Providencia: multiple ANIMAL reservoirs, CATHETER urinary infections. Morganella: like Proteus. Both multidrug resistant.

label: L14 · Salmonella, Shigella, Enteric Yersinia
rows: Salmonella typhi
HUMANS the only host · resists BILE and dyes · fecal food or water (“boil it, cook it, peel it, or forget it”) · chronic GALLBLADDER carriers.
Typhoid course
SMALL intestine → invasive → SEPTICEMIA → liver, spleen; ulceration, PERFORATION. Sustained fever 103–104, ROSE SPOTS. Vaccines: oral (4 doses), injected (1).
Animal salmonelloses
Less severe than typhoid but MORE PREVALENT. Ingestion: POULTRY and EGGS, cattle, REPTILES (pet turtles), backyard flocks. S. cholerae-suis = swine.
Shigella
Fecal food → invades LARGE-intestine villi; does NOT perforate or enter the blood. ENDOTOXIN → fever; ENTEROTOXIN → mucosal damage, blood and mucus. Dysentery; under-5s.
Enteric yersinias
Y. enterocolitica: animals, fish, produce, water; ILEUM inflammation MIMICS APPENDICITIS. Y. pseudotuberculosis: MORE lymph node inflammation.

label: L14 · Yersinia pestis & Plague
rows: Organism
Tiny rod, BIPOLAR staining, capsule · COAGULASE, endotoxin, murine toxin. ~200 rodent reservoirs; United States cases WEST of the Mississippi.
The flea
Coagulase CLOTS block the flea's esophagus → RAVENOUS, bites again → REGURGITATES bacteria into the bite. 3–50 bacilli.
Sylvatic vs urban
SYLVATIC = wild animals · URBAN = domestic or semidomestic animals · human to human rare.
Three forms
BUBONIC: lymph node necrosis, the BUBO (groin, axilla) · SEPTICEMIC: purpura → gangrene, the BLACK plague · PNEUMONIC: lungs, highly contagious by AEROSOL.
Diagnose fast
Death within 2 days of symptoms. History, symptoms, ASPIRATE THE BUBO. Killed or attenuated vaccine (military, vets, lab). QUARANTINE + rodent control.

label: L14 · Pasteurella & Haemophilus
rows: Pasteurella multocida
OXIDASE +; zoonotic, normal ANIMAL flora. Animal BITES or SCRATCHES → local abscess → joints, bones, nodes. Veterinarians; septicemia if immunocompromised.
Haemophilus
“Blood loving,” fastidious. CHOCOLATE agar (cooked blood): needs HEMIN, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) or its phosphate.
H. influenzae
MISNAMED (not the flu). MENINGITIS, EPIGLOTTITIS, otitis media, sinusitis, pneumonia. SUBUNIT vaccine Hib (Haemophilus influenzae type b).
Other species
H. aegyptius: PINK EYE, children, fingers and insects · H. ducreyi: CHANCROID, sexually transmitted · H. parainfluenzae, H. aphrophilus: oral flora → ENDOCARDITIS after dental work.

label: L14 · Objective 2: How We Get Them
rows: Water, soil, equipment
Pseudomonas (biofilms on ventilators, intravenous lines) · B. pseudomallei (injury, inhalation) · Acinetobacter (fomites) · Stenotrophomonas (biofilms).
Animals

Brucella (slaughter, unpasteurized dairy) · Francisella (rabbits, water, dust, vectors) · O157:H7 (cattle) · animal salmonelloses (poultry, eggs, reptiles) · Pasteurella (bites) · plague (fleas, rodents).
Air
Bordetella (carriers, aerosols) · Legionella (water aerosols) · pneumonic plague (aerosol).
Fecal-oral
E. coli diarrheal strains, Salmonella typhi (humans only), Shigella.
Self and partner
E. coli urinary tract infection (women, catheters) · H. parainfluenzae (own oral flora, dental work) · H. ducreyi (sexual) · H. aegyptius (fingers, insects).
